decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to the left tube, lifting and pitching the open left gripper; right arm stays home.
Continue the left elbow-up arc toward the isolated left tube, aligning the approach downward above its middle.
Lower and visually center the open fingers around the left tube, adding a small yaw correction to follow its axis.
Fine-center on the tube body and close the left gripper fully; retention will be checked during a short lift.
Lift the first tube clear of the tabletop with the left gripper closed, retaining the elbow-up branch.
The tube remains between the fingers. Begin a smooth upright rotation while moving toward the left rack slot above the rack.
Finish rotating the retained tube upright over the rack's left side, maintaining clearance before insertion.
Fine-align the upright tube with the left large rack opening and lower toward the slot; keep the grasp closed.
Lower the upright first tube straight into the aligned left rack slot, stopping before release to inspect seating.
The tube appears to have contacted a slot edge and shifted within the fingers. Lift slightly and correct toward the near row before retrying.
Make a small lateral correction over the visible opening, lower gently, then open to let the upright tube settle into the slot.
Withdraw the open left gripper upward and back to inspect whether the first tube stays seated independently.
The first tube remains in the rack after release. Retract left toward home while beginning the right elbow-up approach to the nearer right-side tube.
Continue the right approach over the nearer tube while completing the left arm's open-gripper return toward its origin.
Lower the right open fingers around the nearer tube body, using the wrist view to refine centering and downward alignment.
Center the right grasp slightly nearer the cap and close fully around the tube body before lifting.
Lift the second tube clear with the right gripper closed; check its retention before rotating upright.
The second tube is retained. Rotate it gradually upright while carrying it toward a free right-side rack opening.
Complete the smooth upright rotation above the rack, keeping the second tube securely held and clear of the first.
Bring the second tube closer to the rack with a small upright correction, then inspect the opening alignment before deeper insertion.
Lower the upright second tube slowly toward the free opening, checking for relative tube motion or rim contact.
Continue the second insertion in small vertical increments while watching for contact with the rack rim.
Seat the second tube a few millimeters deeper, open the right fingers, and begin withdrawing without dragging it.
Withdraw the open right gripper upward and away from the second tube, leaving it in the rack before approaching the last tube.
The second tube stays seated. Carry the open right gripper toward the remaining far-right tube while pitching downward along a continuous elbow-up path.
Continue toward the far-right tube with an open downward approach, keeping ample height while the wrist aligns to its length.
Use the right wrist view to center over the last tube and match its slanted axis while lowering the open fingers to grasp height.
Fine-align the last tube's axis in the wrist view, shift slightly toward its cap, and close the right gripper around the body.
Lift the third tube away from the tabletop with a closed right grasp, maintaining the downward wrist orientation until clear.
The last tube is retained. Rotate it upright while carrying it toward an unoccupied central/back rack opening, keeping clear of the seated tubes.
Continue the retained third tube's smooth rotation toward upright above the rack, without descending into neighboring tubes.
Finish the third tube's upright alignment above a free back-row opening, holding height while centering laterally.
Lower the upright third tube toward the back-row opening, keeping the grasp closed and watching clearance from the seated second tube.
Possible gripper interference with the seated tube. Lift clear and shift to the farther-right back opening so the wrist approaches outside its neighbor.
Lower the third tube over the outside back-row opening, monitoring the neighboring tube and keeping the grasp closed.
Continue the third tube's controlled vertical insertion at the outside back slot; inspect seating before opening.
The third tube shifted upward in the fingers on rim contact. Lift it clear and correct slightly toward the nearer side of the back-row hole before retrying.
Gently lower the third tube after the fore-aft correction, adding a small outward centering adjustment over the hole.
Open the right gripper over the corrected slot so the third tube can settle under gravity, then start withdrawing without dragging it.
Withdraw the open right hand to inspect all three tubes independently; seating and uprightness remain visually uncertain.
All three tubes remain at the rack. Begin returning the open right arm to origin while keeping the left arm at its home pose.
The rightmost tube is visibly leaning after release. Approach its upper body again with open fingers to correct its seating rather than declaring completion.
Bring the open right fingers nearer the leaning tube's cap/body junction for a careful corrective regrasp, avoiding the neighboring tube.
Use a small lateral and downward wrist-view correction to bring the leaning tube's cap between the open fingers for a secure regrasp.
Center the leaning tube's cap within the fingers and close for a corrective lift, avoiding additional downward pressure on the rack.
Lift the regrasped cap vertically to free the leaning tube from the rack before correcting its tilt.
The cap is retained. Lift higher and begin rotating the tube's strong lean toward vertical while keeping its tip clear of the rack.
Continue straightening the retained tube from its cap grasp, raising the wrist to preserve tip clearance and positioning above the right rack opening.
Replan after the continuity guard: stop rotating, lower in small increments to reduce reach, and align the visible tube tip with the right back opening.
Correct the remaining leftward tube lean with a small world-axis rotation while easing its tip toward the opening; keep the cap securely held.
The tube now appears straighter. Shift its visible tip outward to the rightmost large opening and approach the rim in submillimeter vertical steps.
